findings.statement: The filing says some customers are developing their own ASICs and other chips, including designs tuned for particular workloads, and warns that competition could lower demand for its products. This supports the direction of the claim, though the passage does not name cloud providers.
findings.rationale: The risk factor states the mechanism (customer-built ASICs for workloads that may not need all of the data center systems' features) and links competitive pressure to lower demand. It is generic risk language: it does not say which customers, how much volume, or that demand has already fallen.

quotes.text: Some of our customers are developing their own ASICs and other products, including designs optimized for certain workloads that may not require all of the features and functionality our data center systems provide.
If we are unable to successfully compete in this environment, demand for our products, services, and technologies could decrease, which may negatively impact our business.

findings.statement: Despite that risk, the latest quarter shows no sign of demand loss in the reported figures: revenue growth was +105.9% year over year, and the business section says all major cloud service providers use its platforms.
findings.rationale: Reported growth shows that any effect from customer-designed accelerators has not yet shown up in total revenue. The figure is company-wide and the business passage is descriptive, so neither isolates cloud-customer GPU demand. They give context, not a test of the claim.

quotes.text: AI model makers use our infrastructure and software hosted at CSPs to develop, build and run AI models, product offerings, and services.

response.rationale: The filings acknowledge that some customers are building their own ASICs and that competition could reduce demand, which supports the claim as a risk. They give no quantification, do not name the big cloud customers, and recent reported growth shows no visible loss, so the claim is supported only as a stated risk.
unknowns: Which customers are developing their own accelerators and whether they are large cloud providers.
How much of data center revenue is exposed to customer-designed chips.
Whether any demand reduction has occurred yet or is only a risk.
The timing and scale of any customer shift to in-house designs.
